t.E414.agn: In 2017 EFSA saw no need for a numerical acceptable daily intake (ADI) and found no safety concern for the general population; it was reported that high amounts may cause flatulence, which was not considered an adverse effect.
t.E414.body: Gum arabic is not absorbed unchanged and is fermented to a small extent by bacteria in the large intestine.
t.E414.eff.0.t: It has been reported to cause flatulence; EFSA did not consider this an adverse effect
t.E414.prod: Obtained by physical means from plant seeds or tree exudate (gum).
t.E414.regx.0: Re-evaluated; no numerical ADI needed, no safety concern for the general population.
t.E414.regx.1: Purity criteria updated (heavy metal limits lowered); from 18.08.2026.
t.E414.summary: A natural gum obtained from the resin of the acacia tree. Used as a flavour carrier and thickener in confectionery, chewing gum and drinks.
t.E414.what: Thickens, stabilises emulsions and slows sugar crystallisation.
